the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of genes that encode key proteins involved in cholesterol metabolism and transport.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SCAP gene is amplified in the SRD-19 cell line, which has been selected for resistance to 25-Hydroxcholesterol.
the Insig-1 gene has been knocked out of the cell line, and the SCAP gene has been amplified.
the SCAP gene has been overexpressed in SRD-14 CHO cells, and this overexpression of SCAP is responsible for the sterol resistance of these cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCAP/Insigs ratio is important in regulating sterol-regulated SREBP processing.

the ratio of the two Insig proteins (Insig-1 and -2) and SREBP cleavage-activator protein (SCAP) determines the sensitivity of cells to the sterol regulatory element binding proteins (SREBPs), which are membrane-bound transcription factors for the genes that encode enzymes for cholesterol and fatty acid biosynthesis.
overexpression of the gene for the SREBP cleavage-activator protein (SCAP) can overcome the effects of Insig- deficiency on sterol-regulated SREBP processing.
